about: Data of case file CF3 (where should hydrogen go when nobody knows how much wind will be built?). Every sentence about the study is approved excerpt wording (E10 and E11), word for word. The toy ('idea') is lesson M8's: its data and plans are read from m08-stochastic-robust.json.

events.label: Journal article (this case)
events.text: Electrolyzers, hydrogen tanks and fuel cells are sized for [[ercot|ERCOT]]'s eight weather zones under uncertain renewable build-out and electricity demand, with hydrogen pipelines between neighboring zones; published online on 2 March 2025, in the March 2025 issue.

source.label: Li et al. (2025), International Journal of Hydrogen Energy 113, 77–89

events.label: Code released
events.text: A documented, runnable implementation of the planning framework, with synthetic examples (version 1.0.2).

boundary.title: Where the result holds
holds: [[ercot|ERCOT]]'s eight weather zones, every hour of one year, in nine scenarios of renewable build-out and electricity demand;
hydrogen demand is held fixed across scenarios;
the CO₂ from gas plants and reformers is captured and stored at a cost;
the emissions result comes from sensitivity runs in which power from gas-fired plants became more expensive.
leaves: truck and rail transport of hydrogen.
boundary.source: From Li et al. (2025), International Journal of Hydrogen Energy.

idea.title: Size it before the wind is built
idea.note: M8's toy: one windy zone, three build-outs with chances 25%, 50% and 25%, illustrative round numbers in 2025 dollars.

plans.label: Plan for the average
plans.def: the best size if the wind built were sure to equal its average, 5,000 MW.

plans.label: Hedged plan
plans.def: the size with the lowest [[expected-value|expected cost]], each build-out's cost weighted by its chance.

plans.label: Worst-case plan
plans.def: the size whose cost in the worst build-out is lowest; it uses no chances.

idea.workedNote: A chance-weighted average: not a guaranteed cost, and not what any one build-out costs.
idea.assumptionsTitle: The toy's assumptions and its wind blocks
assumptions: Surplus wind is free: the electrolyzer pays only its own yearly cost, and wind it does not use is [[curtailment|curtailed]].
The year is five blocks of hours sorted by wind output (a [[duration-curve|duration curve]]), not 8,760 hours in time order.
Industry's hydrogen demand is steady: the same in every hour and every build-out.
One zone: no hydrogen storage, no fuel cells and no pipelines; reformer hydrogen has one fixed price.
idea.blocksCaption: The five wind blocks: the real 2025 hourly wind of the [[spp|Southwest Power Pool (SPP)]], scaled to 33.8%, the 2025 U.S. wind capacity factor, then sorted and cut. The costs above are illustrative.
